patches.title: Keep native MCP access available during long active runs
patches.problem: On the previously inspected nightly, the automatic heartbeat_run MCP token expires after one hour while the provider can still be working.
patches.reason: The earlier public minting API rejects heartbeat_run and adapter access is a frozen credential snapshot; replacement gateway_client or generic sessions do not establish equivalent authority.
patches.owner: Native run preparation and gateway-token lifecycle
patches.proposal: Runtime-owned bounded extension of the same bearer before expiry, only while its run and execution lease are active. Preserve subject, company, agent, gateway/profile, assignments and allowed actions; retain live authorization and atomic terminal revocation.
testsRequired: Existing client remains authorized across the one-hour boundary without restarting
Terminal, cancellation and explicit-revocation races cannot extend authority
Expired or revoked tokens cannot be resurrected
Cross-run, company and gateway/profile isolation; removed permissions remain removed
Lost execution lease and renewal failure preserve bounded expiry and recovery evidence
patches.validation: Contract checks on the old nightly only; no implementation or working-renewal acceptance.
patches.migration: Undetermined until the new nightly contract is reviewed; do not edit production token rows.
patches.rollback: To be specified with the implementation; do not release task reservations or discard collection obligations.
patches.retireWhen: An upstream version provides equivalent active-run continuity, authority boundaries and terminal revocation, confirmed by the same regression cases.
